walkthroughs.body_html:
Readers, Writers and Texts — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Readers, Writers and Texts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Readers, Writers and Texts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term unreliable narrator in 1961?
options: Wayne Booth
Northrop Frye
F R Leavis
Mikhail Bakhtin

mcqs.q: Which Marquez novel exemplifies magic realism?
options: Love in the Time of Cholera
One Hundred Years of Solitude
The Autumn of the Patriarch
Chronicle of a Death Foretold
A bildungsroman is a novel about constructing buildings.
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
An unreliable narrator is one who tells lies in the story.
Their account is undermined within the text by ignorance, bias, self-deception or deceit, so the reader must read against what they say.

mcqs.q: What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Gothic just means scary stories with vampires and ghosts.
A novel tracing a protagonist's moral and psychological development from youth to adulthood — typically involving formative experiences and a clearer sense of self.
A bildungsroman is a novel about constructing buildings.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
Any novel with a young protagonist is a bildungsroman.
